 ----Appellants  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Appellant(s) : Mr. Vineet Jain, Senior Advocate,
 assisted by Mr. Praveen Vyas For Respondent(s) : Mr. Abhishek Purohit,
AGA  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Judgment 18/09/2023 1.

The appellants have preferred the instant criminal appeal under Section 449 of the CrPC being aggrieved of the order dated 26.07.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Jaitaran,
District Pali in Criminal Case No.17/2022, whereby the learned court below ordered forfeiture of the complete amount of surety bonds and personal bond of the accused.
2. Facts relevant and essential for disposal of the case are that the appellant No.3 Sandeep Gupta is facing trial for the commission of offences under Sections 285, 379, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC, Section 3 of the PDPP Act, Sections [2023:RJ-JD:32432] (2 of 5) [CRLAS-1932/2023]
15(2)(4), 16 of P & MP Act and Section 3/4 of the Explosive Substance Act in connection with FIR No.308/2020 registered at the Police Station Raipur, District Pali.

sentences.text: During trial, the appellant No.3 preferred an application seeking temporary bail, which was allowed by this court vide order dated 06.07.2022 granting temporary bail for 15 days subject to deposition of Rs.2,50,000/- with the trial court and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.4,00,000/- and two sureties in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- each, with a stipulation that the amount of Rs.2,50,000/- would be refunded to the appellant No.3 upon surrender, else the same shall stand fortified.
The appellant No.3 was released on bail upon fulfilling the above conditions and the appellant No.1 and 2 stood as surety for him.

After being released on bail, the appellant No.3 did not surrender before the authorities within the stipulated time and therefore, his bail bonds were forfeited and proceedings under Section 446 were initiated.
The appellants submitted replies in the proceedings under Section 446 of the CrPC.
The learned court below vide order dated 26.07.2023 directed forfeiture of the complete amount of surety bonds of the appellant No.1 and 2 and personal bond of the appellant No.3.
Being aggrieved of the said order, the instant appeal has been preferred.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the learned court below has failed to take into account the relevant facts and circumstances due to which the appellant No.3 failed to comply with the conditions of the bail order.

It is submitted that the [2023:RJ-JD:32432] (3 of 5)
[CRLAS-1932/2023] appellant No.3 was suffering from a financial crisis and his wife was suffering from a serious ailment.
During the period of temporary bail, the health condition of the appellant's wife worsened and he could not surrender back.
Later on he was arrested by Gujarat Police in connection with other case and brought before the trial court through production warrant.
So far as the appellant No.1-surety is concerned, he was not in India during the relevant time.
The appellant No.2-surety tried his best to search and make the appellant No.3 surrender before the authorities.

It is submitted that the purpose of conducting proceedings under Section 446 of the CrPC is to determine quantum of forfeiture of the bonds, but the learned court below in a mechanical manner ordered forfeiture of complete amount of bonds.

Hence, it is prayed that taking a lenient view, the amount of forfeiture of bonds may be reduced suitably specially looking to the fact that the amount of Rs.2,50,000/- at the time of release on temporary bail has already been forfeited.
5. Per contra, the learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the appellants and submits that no interference is called for in the order impugned.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
7.

In the cases where breach of conditions of bail bonds is alleged under Section 446 of the CrPC, the court has to consider [2023:RJ-JD:32432] (4 of 5) [CRLAS-1932/2023] various factors before determining the quantum of forfeiture of bond amount.
Section 446 (3) provides that the court is not required to direct the payment or recovery of whole of the bond amount.
It is well within its right to remit some portion of the amount after recording reasons for doing so.

Reasons can be several, like conduct of the accused and the sureties, their economic capacity of payment,
circumstances which led to breach of conditions etc.

In the case at hand, the reasons assigned for breach of conditions of bail bonds are that the wife of the appellant No.3 was suffering from some ailment and as her health deteriorated during the period of temporary bail, the accused could not surrender; the financial status of the accused was weakened; later on he was arrested by Gujarat Anant Goyal vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:Rj-Jd:32432) on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154241942/
2 Police and was brought on production warrant.

sentences.text: One of the surety is reported to be out of country at the relevant time and the other surety has stated that he was bonafidely trying to get the accused surrendered and did not act irresponsibly and there was no connivance or negligence on his part.
I have pondered over the reasons given by the accused and the sureties and am convinced with the same.

Apart from that, I have also taken into account the fact that the amount of Rs.2,50,000/-
deposited by the accused at the time of release has already been forfeited.

8. In the over all facts and circumstances of the case, considering the financial condition of the accused and the sureties, their conduct and reasons which led the accused to breach the conditions of bail, taking a humanitarian approach, this court is inclined to exercise leniency in favour of the appellants.
[2023:RJ-JD:32432] (5 of 5) [CRLAS-1932/2023
] Accordingly, the impugned order dated 26.07.2023 is modified in the manner that only 10% of bond amounts shall be forfeited and the rest of the amount shall be remitted.

The appellant No.1 and 2 shall deposit an amount of Rs.20,000/-
each and the appellant No.3 shall deposit an amount of Rs.40,000/- with the trial court within a reasonable time.
9. The appeal is allowed in these terms.

Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
(FARJAND ALI),J 228-Pramod/-
